'''Mae-Wan Ho''' ({{zh|c=何梅灣|p=Hé Méiwān}}; 12 November 1941 – 24 March 2016)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bangmosnow.com/2016/05/20/in-memory-dr-mae-wan-ho-ban-gmos-now/ |title=In Memory of Dr. Mae-Wan Ho |work=Ban GMOs Now |date=20 May 2016 |accessdate=21 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161222090003/https://bangmosnow.com/2016/05/20/in-memory-dr-mae-wan-ho-ban-gmos-now/ |archive-date=22 December 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was a [[geneticist]]<ref>Polly Curtis, "Exploitation on the agenda at ethics forum", ''The Guardian'', 22 February 2002. [https://www.theguardian.com/education/2002/feb/22/research.highereducation Reprint]. Accessed 9 June 2008.</ref><ref name="Independent Science Panel">[http://www.indsp.org/MWHcv.php Independent Science Panel] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080707034050/http://www.indsp.org/MWHcv.php |date=7 July 2008 }} CURRICULUM VITAE of Mae-Wan Ho</ref> known for her critical views on [[genetic engineering]] and [[evolution]].<ref name="Dr. Mae-Wan Ho bio">[http://www.bio.davidson.edu/people/kabernd/seminar/2004/GMbios/MT.html Davidson College] Dr. Mae-Wan Ho bio</ref><ref>Tim Gardam, Director of programmes, Channel 4, "Seeds of discontent at C4", ''The Guardian'', 18 March 2000. [https://www.theguardian.com/theguardian/2000/mar/18/guardianletters3 Reprint]. Accessed 9 June 2008.</ref> She authored or co-authored a number of publications, including 10 books, such as ''The Rainbow and the Worm, the Physics of Organisms'' (1993, 1998), ''Genetic Engineering: Dream or Nightmare?'' (1998, 1999), ''Living with the Fluid Genome'' (2003) and ''Living Rainbow H<sub>2</sub>O'' (2012).	
[[File:Mae-wan ho interference (720p)-00.00.13.030-00.02.10.820.webm|thumb|300px|Interview with Ho on [[electromagnetic fields]] (02:01min) ]]

Ho was criticized for embracing [[pseudoscience]].<ref>[http://www.agbioworld.org/newsletter_wm/index.php?caseid=archive&newsid=406 "Mae-Wan Ho"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304051431/http://www.agbioworld.org/newsletter_wm/index.php?caseid=archive&newsid=406 |date=4 March 2016 }}. Retrieved 24 April 2014.</ref><ref name="Colquhoun">{{cite web |last=Colquhoun |first=David |title=Institute of Science in Society: beware! |url=http://www.dcscience.net/?p=129 |work=DC's Improbable Science |date=19 July 2006 |accessdate=26 December 2012 |authorlink=David Colquhoun}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Ho received a PhD in biochemistry in 1967 from [[Hong Kong University]], was postdoctoral fellow in biochemical genetics, [[University of California, San Diego]], from 1968 to 1972, senior research fellow in [[Queen Elizabeth College]], lecturer in genetics (from 1976) and [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]] in biology (from 1985) in the [[Open University]], and since retiring in June 2000 visiting professor of biophysics in [[Catania University]], [[Sicily]].<ref name="Independent Science Panel"/><ref name="Dr. Mae-Wan Ho bio"/>

Ho died of cancer in March 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.samburcher.com/articles/public-health/109-tribute-to-dr-mae-wan-ho-1941-2016.html|title = Articles}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wessex.ac.uk/news/general-news/910-obituary-mae-wan-ho |title=Obituary - Mae-Wan Ho |access-date=3 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805062037/http://www.wessex.ac.uk/news/general-news/910-obituary-mae-wan-ho |archive-date=5 August 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Institute of Science in Society ==
Ho was a co-founder and director of the Institute of Science in Society (ISIS), an [[Advocacy group|interest group]] which published fringe articles about climate change, GMOs, [[homeopathy]], traditional Chinese medicine, and [[water memory]]. In reviewing the organisation, [[David Colquhoun]] accused the ISIS of promoting [[pseudoscience]] and specifically criticised Ho's understanding of [[homeopathy]].<ref name="Colquhoun"/>

The institute is on the [[Quackwatch]] list of questionable organizations.<ref>{{cite web|last=Barrett|first=Stephen|title=Questionable Organizations: An Overview|url=http://www.quackwatch.org/04ConsumerEducation/nonrecorg.html|publisher=[[Quackwatch]]|accessdate=14 October 2013}}</ref>

== Genetic engineering ==
Ho, together with Joe Cummins of the [[University of Western Ontario]], has argued that a sterility gene engineered into a crop could be transferred to other crops or wild relatives and that "This could severely compromise the agronomic performance of conventional crops and cause wild relatives to go extinct". They argued that this process could also produce genetic instabilities, which might be "leading to catastrophic breakdown", and stated that there are no data to assure that this has not happened or cannot happen.<ref>Donald MacLeod, "Who's listening? Will public opinion on genetically modified crops make any difference to the government?", ''The Guardian'', 19 May 2003. [https://www.theguardian.com/science/2003/may/19/gm.food Reprint]. Accessed 9 June 2008.</ref> This concern contrasts with the reason why these sterile plants were developed, which was to prevent the transfer of genes to the environment by preventing any plants that are bred with or that receive these genes from reproducing.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Daniell H |title=Molecular strategies for gene containment in transgenic crops |journal=Nat. Biotechnol. |volume=20 |issue=6 |pages=581–6 |date=June 2002 |pmid=12042861 |doi=10.1038/nbt0602-581 |pmc=3471138}}</ref> Indeed, any gene that caused sterility when transferred to a new species would be eliminated by [[natural selection]] and could not spread.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Lee D, Natesan E |title=Evaluating genetic containment strategies for transgenic plants |journal=Trends Biotechnol. |volume=24 |issue=3 |pages=109–14 |date=March 2006 |pmid=16460821 |doi=10.1016/j.tibtech.2006.01.006}}</ref>

Ho expressed concerns about the spread of altered genes through [[horizontal gene transfer]] and that the experimental alteration of genetic structures may be out of control. One of her concerns is that the [[antibiotic resistance|antibiotic resistant]] gene that was isolated from bacteria and used in some [[Genetically modified food|GM crops]] might cross back from plants by [[horizontal gene transfer]] to different species of bacteria, because "If this happened it would leave us unable to treat major illnesses like [[meningitis]] and ''[[Escherichia coli|E coli]]''."<ref>Antony Barnett, "GM genes 'jump species barrier', GM food: special report", ''The Guardian'', 28 May 2000. [https://www.theguardian.com/science/2000/may/28/gm.food Reprint]. Accessed 9 June 2008.</ref> Her views were published in an opinion article based on a review of others' research.<ref name=Ho1999>{{cite journal
 | author = Ho, M.W. |author2=Ryan, A. |author3=Cummins, J. | year = 1999 | title = Cauliflower Mosaic Viral Promoter-A Recipe for Disaster? | journal = Microbial Ecology in Health and Disease | volume = 11 | issue = 4 | pages = 194–197 | url = http://www.informaworld.com/index/M8H21H3GTNX7A4FR.pdf  | accessdate = 10 June 2008 | doi=10.3402/mehd.v11i4.7918}}</ref> The arguments and conclusions of this article were heavily criticized by prominent plant scientists,<ref>
{{cite journal
|title=Scientists avert new GMO crisis - Nature Biotechnology
|journal=Nature Biotechnology
|date=January 2000
|volume=18
|issue=1
|pages=13
|publisher=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]
|doi=10.1038/71838
|last1=Hodgson
|first1=John
|pmid=10625373
|s2cid=30792458
|doi-access=free
}}
</ref> and the claims of the article criticized in detail in a response that was published in the same journal,<ref name=Hull2000>{{cite journal | author = Hull, R. |author2=Covey, S.N. |author3=Dale, P. | year = 2000 | title = Genetically modified plants and the 35S promoter: assessing the risks and enhancing the debate | journal = Microbial Ecology in Health and Disease | volume = 12 | issue = 1 | pages = 1–5 | doi = 10.1080/089106000435527|s2cid=218565785 | doi-access = free }} {{Dead link|date=November 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref> prompting a reply from Ho.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1080/089106000435536-1|title=Hazards of transgenic plants containing the cauliflower mosaic viral promoter: Authors' reply to critiques of "The Cauliflower Mosaic Viral Promoter - a Recipe for Disaster?"|journal=Microbial Ecology in Health and Disease|volume=12|pages=6–11|year=2000|last1=Ho|first1=Mae-Wan|s2cid=86135285|doi-access=free}}</ref> A review on the topic published in 2008 in the ''Annual Review of Plant Biology'' stated that ''"These speculations have been extensively rebutted by the scientific community"''.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Lemaux PG |title=Genetically Engineered Plants and Foods: A Scientist's Analysis of the Issues (Part I) |journal=Annu Rev Plant Biol |volume=59 |pages=771–812 |year=2008 |pmid=18284373 |doi=10.1146/annurev.arplant.58.032806.103840}}</ref>
Indeed, at the launch of her 1998 book ''Genetic Engineering Dream or Nightmare?'' (held in the very room in which the first reading of Darwin´s ''On The Origin of Species'' had been given in 1860!) opposing her was John Durant, Professor of Public Understanding of Science at Imperial College, London.
At a dinner afterwards - and Ho already a grandmother - the Professor came to blows with her.{{cn|date=July 2026}}

Ho has also argued that bacteria could acquire the bacterial gene [[barnase]] from transgenic plants. This gene kills any cell that expresses it and lacks [[barstar]], the specific inhibitor of barnase activity. In an article entitled ''Chronicle of An Ecological Disaster Foretold'', which was published in an ISIS newsletter, Ho speculated that if a bacterium acquired the barnase gene and survived, this could make the bacteria a more dangerous pathogen.{{cn|date=July 2026}}

==Evolution==

Ho has claimed that evolution is pluralistic because there are many mechanisms that can produce variation in phenotypes independently of haphazard mutations. Ho has advocated a form of [[Lamarckism|Lamarckian]] evolution. She has been criticized by the [[scientific community]] for setting up [[straw man]] arguments in her criticism of natural selection and supporting discredited evolutionary theories.<ref>[[Douglas J. Futuyma|J. Futuyma, Douglas]]. (1984). ''Neo-Darwinism in Disfavor''. ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''. New Series, Vol. 226, No. 4674. pp. 532-533.</ref><ref>[[Michael Ghiselin|Ghiselin, Michael]]. (1985). ''Evolutionary Theory: Paths into the Future by J. W. Pollard; Beyond Neo-Darwinism: An Introduction to the New Evolutionary Paradigm by Mae-Wan Ho; Peter T. Saunders''. ''[[American Scientist]]''. Vol. 73, No. 6. p. 584.</ref><ref>[[G. Ledyard Stebbins|Stebbins, G. Ledyard]]. (1985). ''A New Approach to Research on Evolution?''. ''[[BioScience]]''. Vol. 35, No. 8. pp. 514-516.</ref><ref>[[Joseph Felsenstein|Felsenstein, Joseph]]. (1986). ''Waiting for Post-Neo-Darwin''. ''[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]]''. Vol. 40, No. 4. pp. 883-889.</ref><ref>Wake, Marvalee H.(1986). ''Beyond Neo-Darwinism. An Introduction to the New Evolutionary Paradigm by Mae-Wan Ho; Peter T. Saunders''. ''[[Integrative and Comparative Biology|American Zoologist]]''. Vol. 26, No. 1 (1986), pp. 289-290.</ref><ref>[[Mark Pagel|Pagel, Mark]]. (1989). ''Evolutionary Processes and Metaphors by Mae-Wan Ho; Sidney W. Fox''. ''[[Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute|Man]]''. New Series, Vol. 24, No. 4. pp. 689-690.</ref> But some of her Lamarckian ideas have since entered the mainstream of the evolutionary literature.<ref>J. [[James A. Shapiro]] "Evolution: a view from the 21st Century (2011)" [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273335226_Evolution_a_view_from_the_21st_century]</ref><ref>[[Eva Jablonka]] "Evolution in Four Dimensions" [{{ISBN|0-262-10107-6}}]</ref>

The paleontologist [[Philip D. Gingerich|Philip Gingerich]] has noted that Ho's evolutionary ideas are based on [[Vitalism|vitalistic]] thinking.<ref>[[Philip D. Gingerich|Gingerich, Philip D]]. (1989). ''New Vitalism in Evolution: Evolutionary Processes and Metaphors M.-W. Ho S. W. Fox''. ''[[BioScience]]'' 39: 195-196.</ref>
